title: Bernoulli restriction cost, asymptotic version
statement:
Fix a parameter $p$ with $0 < p \le 1$, positive integers $w, s > 0$, and a tolerance $\varepsilon > 0$. Then there exists $N \in \bbn$ such that for every $n \ge N$ with $n > 0$ and every decidable event on restrictions of $n$ variables, the following holds: if the fixed-size restriction probability satisfies
\[
  R_k[\mathrm{event}] \le \left(\frac{5\,k\,w}{n}\right)^{s} \qquad \text{for every } k \le n,
\]
then the probability of the event under a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction satisfies
\[
  \Pr_{p}[\mathrm{event}] \le (10\,p\,w)^{s} + \varepsilon.
\]
hypotheses_covered: event is a decidable predicate on restrictions of n variables
for all k ≤ n, fixed-size restriction probability R_k[event] ≤ (5kw/n)^s
replaced:
